findings.passage: “In the aftermath of the horrific shooting in Parkland, Florida, I watched as those brave students from Stoneman Douglas High School stood in the balcony watching while the Florida Legislature did nothing,” said Treasurer Deb Goldberg. “It is clear that traditional approaches have not worked. Divesting our public pension funds from gun and ammunition manufacturers sends a clear message that we stand with the victims and survivors of gun violence everywhere.”
findings.note: Treasury press release quoting her on a bill to make the state pension fund sell shares in gun and ammunition makers.

findings.passage: “It is unacceptable that we as a country continue to live in a seemingly endless cycle of gun violence,” Goldberg said in a statement. “Traditional approaches are not working, and we must do what we can to potentially save lives.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Eagle-Tribune (article date) when she urged lawmakers to direct the pension fund to divest from firearm and ammunition companies after the Uvalde and Buffalo shootings. Article text was read from the page source.

findings.passage: “While I am personally against owning gun stocks,’’ Goldberg said in a statement in the wake of the Orlando nightclub massacre Sunday, divestment from the state fund “has to be a directive from the Legislature.”
findings.note: Boston Globe (hosted on mass.gov) quoting her statement that divesting the pension fund from gun stocks needs a legislative directive.

findings.motion: Treasurer-backed bill filed, H.4402/S.2407, pension divestment from ammunition and firearms
findings.note: She announced the filing of a bill (sponsored by a state representative and a state senator) requiring the pension board to sell shares in firearm and ammunition makers earning 15% or more of revenue from civilian sales. She is not the legislative sponsor; instrument number taken from her 2018 testimony page.

findings.motion: Letter of testimony supporting H.4402 and S.2407, pension divestment from ammunition and firearms
findings.note: Her office posted her letter of testimony in support of the two divestment bills. The letter file itself had no readable text.

findings.motion: Treasury fact sheet for H.55, pension divestment from ammunition and firearms
findings.note: Fact sheet from her office says the Treasurer again proposes divestment of pension holdings in gun and ammunition firms; year inferred only from the September 2019 figures in it.

findings.motion: Request to add firearm-divestment language to the supplemental budget bill; she also filed a standalone divestment bill that was sent to study
findings.note: News report says she asked lawmakers to add divestment of firearm and ammunition makers to a pending budget bill and had filed a standalone bill earlier in the session. Date is the article date.
